title: Unify fallback policy adapters and async iterator helpers
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: - Add FallbackPolicyAdapter to unify credential fallback across SDKs; - Add async iterator helpers to standardize streaming ergonomics; - Bump python SDK to v1.12.0; - Update docs and add targeted tests.
description: Context: multiple SDK teams have drifted on how credential fallback and streaming iterables behave; this PR introduces a small protocol and concrete 'FallbackPolicyAdapter' plus a compact set of async iterator helpers to make stream consumption ergonomic and consistent across Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs. Motivation: reduce duplicated fallback logic in user apps, enable parity with TS/Go ergonomics, and provide safer defaults for transient auth errors. What this PR does: implements FallbackPolicyAdapter with pluggable strategies (primary->prefetch->delegated), adds AsyncStreamHelpers for line-buffered and chunked stream consumption with deterministic cancellation semantics, adds a small compatibility shim to align behavior with TS/Go SDKs, and bumps python package version to 1.12.0. Checklist: - [x] Implement adapter interface and default implementations. - [x] Add unit tests exercising TTL edge cases and prefetch behavior. - [x] Add async iterator helpers and integration test with streaming endpoint emulator. - [x] Update docs/streaming.md and CHANGELOG. - [x] Coordinate with redwood-sdk-typescript and redwood-sdk-go for naming parity (ENG-5124). Commits summary: feat: add FallbackPolicyAdapter interface and default policy; feat: async iterator helpers (chunked, line_buffered, with_cancel); fix: handle credential refresh race when TTL ~0; test: coverage for fallback strategies and iterator cancellation; chore: bump py package to 1.12.0 and update changelog. Files changed (high level): src/redwood/auth/fallback.py - core adapter and strategies. src/redwood/stream/async_helpers.py - async iterator helpers and docstrings. src/redwood/__init__.py - version bump. tests/test_fallback.py tests/test_async_helpers.py docs/streaming.md CHANGELOG.md pyproject.toml. Review: Liam O'Connor: "Nice extraction; can we avoid exposing strategy internals in the public API? Suggest exposing only register_policy(name, factory) and keep concrete strategy classes private." Maya Chen (author): "Agree, updated public factory surface — concrete classes moved under _strategies and only factories exposed." Priya Nair: "Can we add a short example for consuming large streaming responses with backpressure-aware iterator?" Maya Chen: "Added example and a short snippet in docs/streaming.md that demonstrates chunked consumption and graceful cancel." Jonas Müller: "I ran stress tests; one codepath in the prefetch policy showed a small memory leak when cancel is called immediately after first chunk. Please add a guard." Maya Chen: "Added an explicit cancellation guard and new integration test that reproduces the scenario; stress run passed locally." CI summary: initial CI run reported a flaky test in tests/test_async_helpers.py (timing-sensitive). I adjusted test to use deterministic asyncio loop advance and retriggered pipelines. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, type-check). Cross-repo coordination: opened a companion PR in redwood-sdk-typescript to mirror naming and surfaces; flagged for sync in ENG-5124. Backwards compatibility notes: default policy remains the simple 'primary' behavior; advanced fallback must be opt-in via client configuration. No breaking changes expected. Merge: squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-26 after approvals from Liam, Priya, and Jonas. Post-merge: published v1.12.0 wheel to internal artifact registry and updated internal integration tests for a downstream service that had brittle fallback assumptions.
